mission: Build the native ShortForge Editor page and safely connect existing generated Shorts

okf.summary: Architecture and code paths reviewed. Follow-up is required because legacy jobs lack a guaranteed editable source manifest and export is intentionally disabled.

forgers.name: product-design
findings: Generation READY panel and Media Library route to a dedicated editor page.
Legacy flattened imports are clearly labelled and do not claim recovered scene/question layers.

forgers.name: editor-runtime
findings: Existing CompositionIR and DurableEditor are reused.
CAS sources are resolved server-side and actual bytes are hash checked before compilation.
A regression test covers successful CAS resolution and tamper rejection.

forgers.name: render-security
findings: A dedicated editor playback route now verifies session, job ownership, source binding, byte length and SHA-256.
No production export endpoint is exposed by this change; export remains locked pending worker input staging, Treasury admission, F06 output and F07 evidence.

security.notes: Code-path controls were added, but automated security scans and browser/API adversarial tests have not yet qualified this feature.

proposedResolutions.proposal: Keep export disabled until F05 source manifest, worker-side source staging/hash validation, server-authorized Treasury, F06 render, CAS output and F07 receipt are integrated and tested.
Import old completed MP4s as one explicitly labelled clip. Do not invent original scenes, question data, captions, or independent narration.
Use external editor repositories as feature/architecture references. Review all licenses before vendoring or adding dependencies.

acceptedResolutions.resolution: Reuse CompositionIR, DurableEditor and the existing Studio rather than creating a competing timeline runtime.
Use an authenticated owner-bound playback endpoint and verify the physical CAS digest before serving source bytes.

finalDisposition.reason: The draft implementation has not passed full CI/E2E/security qualification, and true scene-level editing still depends on a persistent F05/F06 source manifest.
